chapter: Jelly Roll, Leonard Reed and Chicago mixed crowds
title: Leonard Reed's show and Francois's expanded band
summary: He tells about Leonard Reed's chorus and the Harlem Opera House run, and the twelve-piece band.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Now, there's one thing I've never told you about. He had a fellow named Leonard Reed. I don't know if you've ever heard of him. Can't place him now. Well, he's a show producer. He used to be a tap dancer a long time ago. Real light boy. But he got up on one of the best shows in Chicago ever was known. He was a guy named Dave, Dave, Dave, Dave, Riley, Dave Sutton. He used to be a gangster. But then how he had the swing land in Chicago. And he thought more Leonard Reed needed his own son. Leonard Reed wasn't no kin to him. But he was just crazy about Leonard Reed. And he gave Leonard Reed preference to build that show up. And if he get that show like he wanted it, he was going to let Leonard Reed take it anywhere he wanted. So Leonard Reed got that show down like he wanted and took it to New York. And that's the first chorus in my life I've ever seen get them claws, you know. Come back three times, back on the stage and dance three times. Uncores. Uncores, yeah. That's the first chorus I've ever seen do it. And there's a number one chorus in New York and number two is supposed to be hot. But these girls cleaned up for him. These girls cleaned up for him. Boy, I mean he had a chorus out of the books. Boy, them girls really could dance together. And a girl made a misstep on nothing no time. I'm telling you. And Leonard Reed, that was his name. We went to New York and worked at the Harlem Opera House. Went there for one week and stood there two months. Yeah, he stood there two months with that show. And then you know how it is in them towns. The guy get this girl over there and tell him what he'd pay off of. You know, and pay him more than Leonard. And the guy get another girl. And them girls went just like that. Different parts of the state of New York. Two of them went on over in England or somewhere. They're over there yet. Didn't got to be old women. They're over there yet. Yeah, but he had a short old boy.
Well, this must have been a while back.
Oh yeah, this was back there in the, 32, 31, 30 long in the day.
Yeah, that's the band we was with.
But we had to build the band up. See, we had to put about, let's see, we had six pieces. And he put six more pieces in the band. Made a 12 piece of band. That's what we had to have.

Well, Al Wynn was one. I was one. Francois and Duke El, Duke Caston. I mean, his name is Charles Duke Caston, but we called him Duke. And he had Lawrence Brown on tenor, Robert Crowder on tenor, Fred Howard on alto and clarinet. And he had Clowns, Clowns Brown on piano. He had me, I'm trying to think of these trumpet players now. I forget that boy's name. But I mean, I mean anyhow, well, Hopkin went off with us. Hopkin and me and another little young trumpet, he's younger than us, but he could play a lot and he was, you know, using him for the high notes. And I was doing the getting off.
You named the tuba player or bass player?
Oh yeah, William Hillion. Same guy, huh? Yeah, he was the tuba player.
I have to play that record for you sometime.
Golden Lily and somebody stole my gas.
Well, Duke Caston was on guitar.
